shared_context.topic: anti-nausea medications to allow fluids to stay down (enumeration of antiemetics)

snippets.output: There are several anti-nausea medications that can help alleviate nausea and vomiting, making it easier to keep fluids down.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of properties of anti-nausea medications: they alleviate nausea/vomiting and help keep fluids down.

snippets.output: Metoclopramide is a commonly used medication for alleviating nausea and vomiting; it works by blocking dopamine receptors in the brain, which helps to reduce nausea and vomiting.
snippets.pattern_notes: Mechanism causal chain: blocks dopamine receptors -> reduces nausea/vomiting, attached to metoclopramide.

snippets.output: Ondansetron is a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist effective in preventing nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of ondansetron properties: drug class plus parallel indications (chemo, radiation, surgery).

snippets.output: Ondansetron is often used in combination with other medications, such as dexamethasone, to enhance its anti-nausea effects.
snippets.pattern_notes: Combination with dexamethasone presented as the means to enhance anti-nausea effects—conditional/causal extension.

snippets.output: Promethazine and prochlorperazine can be used to treat nausea and vomiting, although they may have more sedative effects.
snippets.notes: Promethazine and prochlorperazine grouped together because the source text presents them jointly with a shared sedative-effects property (Pattern A on a co-described pair).
snippets.pattern_notes: Explicit Pattern A in notes: pair grouped with shared sedative-effects property.

snippets.output: It is essential to consult a healthcare professional to determine the best medication for your specific needs and to discuss any potential side effects or interactions with other medications.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of parallel recommendations to consult a healthcare professional (best medication choice; side effects/interactions).
